stories.title: Is Pakhtunkhwa stuck between a rock and a hard place?
summary: In the centre’s version of events, this mandate was used to flagrantly launch attacks; in PTI’s version, its government in KP was the last line of defence against excesses and power grabs.
The advisory council, governor, and federal government should rest assured that every single move over the next few months will be closely scrutinised.

And if subjective disapproval of a government’s performance is accepted as sufficient grounds for doing away with democracy, then all elected governments in Pakistan—provincial and federal—will rue the day.

stories.title: Lahore police chief denies Fazl’s arrest
summary: Fazl’s late-night claim of his arrest came as authorities barred him and eight other leaders of his party from entering, residing or remaining in Sargodha — where the JUI-F planned to hold a rally on Thursday — for 30 days.
In the video posted on the JUI-F’s X account, Fazl asked his party workers and supporters to postpone protests and sit-ins.
Fazl-govt rift On Tuesday, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman claimed he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

stories.title: Erdogan completes Turkiye's ratification of Makkah defence pact
summary: President Tayyip Erdogan has formally approved the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the country’s Official Gazette said on Friday, completing Turkiye’s ratification after parliament ratified it earlier this month.

The approval comes as Pakistan hosts a two-day meeting of the tripartite alliance’s top decision-making body from Friday, with discussions also expected to feature the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi fighters.

Managing relations with Iran will be particularly important for Pakistan, which has sought to preserve diplomatic engagement with Tehran while deepening defence cooperation with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

stories.title: Islamabad set to host Makkah Defence Alliance meeting today; Yemen conflict also on agenda
summary: Pakistan is set to host a two-day meeting of the tripartite Makkah Defence Alliance’s top decision-making body from today, with discussions also expected to feature the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi fighters in Yemen.
The alliance The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on Aug 7.

Managing relations with Iran will be particularly important for Pakistan, which has sought to preserve diplomatic engagement with Tehran while deepening defence cooperation with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

stories.title: ASI demoted, Golra SHO’s pay cut over flawed theft probe
summary: ISLAMABAD: An investigation officer (IO) was demoted and a station house officer (SHO) faced a two-stage reduction in pay for poor investigation and supervision of a theft case, a police official said on Wednesday.
The IO, an assistant sub-inspector (ASI), was demoted to the rank of head constable, while the pay of the SHO of Golra Police Station was reduced by two stages.

DIG Islamabad Ali Wasim emphasised that all officers must perform their duties with dedication and ensure effective coordination to control crime and maintain law and order. “Protection of citizens’ lives and property is the foremost priority of Islamabad Police,” he said.

stories.title: LHC seeks replies on plea by five Afghan medical students over MBBS registration
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday issued notices to the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) and other respondents on a petition filed by five Afghan medical students seeking registration to sit their first professional MBBS examination in January.
In September, the LHC suspended the operation of PMDC directives ordering Afghan medical students to return to Afghanistan.

The PMDC barred medical and dental colleges from admitting or placing Afghan students for the current academic session and said those already enrolled in such programmes were required to return to Afghanistan.

stories.title: 'Construction continued in broad daylight': Residents see greed, official negligence behind Baloch Colony building collapse
summary: 'Construction continued in broad daylight': Residents see greed, official negligence behind Baloch Colony building collapse

stories.title: Who Controls America’s AI Chokepoint?
summary: Senator Kevin Cramer has warned that while Nvidia’s board has assumed the legal and reputational risks of reinstating Huang, the national-security risks fall on the American military and public.
American AI dominance gives the US leverage over China, but the US economy’s dependence on Nvidia has created a second, domestic chokepoint.
The US has the power to restrict foreign access to American technology, but such restrictions obviously affect Nvidia’s bottom line.

stories.title: PHC stays arrest, deportation of Afghan house officers
summary: Allows them to continue training at Ayub Medical College They also sought directions to the PMDC to issue provisional registration certificates or licences to enable them to undertake and complete their mandatory one-year paid house job training.

The lawyer said the petitioners were aggrieved by the “unlawful” interruption of their house job training following the impugned letters issued by the PMDC, which required Afghan medical students and trainee doctors to return to Afghanistan immediately.

He said the PMDC had issued one of the impugned letters on Oct 7, circulating a directive from the Prime Minister’s Office that directed all medical and dental institutions to terminate or not offer house jobs to Afghan students and required them to leave Pakistan by Oct 10.

stories.title: PPRA points out procedural flaw in CDA’s sewage treatment plants
summary: A joint venture of Elite Engineering - Orient Water Technologies - approached PPRA against the Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC) of the CDA for dismissing their applications.

After a hearing, three-member committee headed by PPRA Managing Director Hasnat Ahmed Qureshi pointed out that GRC had failed to record a satisfactory and reasoned determination regarding the disclosure issue despite having considered the matter during its proceedings.

A former member of the CDA, speaking to Dawn, said there should be proper networking for the plants to avoid sludge, silt and solid material, adding heavy silt can settle inside the treatment units, disturbing the biological treatment process.

stories.title: Making waves: Pakistani woman breaking jet ski barriers
summary: This photograph taken on October 24, 2026 shows visitors gather for jet ski and boat rides at the Kallar Kahar Lake in Pakistan’s Chakwal district. —AFP “Some said ‘You’re a woman, how will you work among men?’” she added.

This photograph taken on October 24, 2026 shows visitors riding a boat in the waters of Kallar Kahar Lake in Pakistan’s Chakwal district.—AFP Ever since Jabeen joined, “it has become completely easy for us to send women to ride” with her, he told AFP.
Header image: Farhat Jabeen (rear) takes a visitor for a spin on a jet ski across the waters of Kallar Kahar Lake in Chakwal district.—AFP

stories.title: Punjab releases Rs1.2bn to acquire land for Punjab University campus in Gujar Khan
summary: GUJAR KHAN: The Punjab government has sanctioned and released Rs1.2 billion for the purchase of land for the establishment of the Potohar campus of the University of the Punjab in Gujar Khan.
According to Raja Pervez Ashraf, an area of over 800 kanals owned by the district government was selected for the establishment of the university campus on GT Road near Gujar Khan.
The officer said the approval of funds for the purchase of land for the Potohar campus had been welcomed by students and the university management, who expressed their gratitude to the government.

stories.title: Funeral prayers of eight more Libya boat tragedy victims offered in Bajaur
summary: The joint funeral prayers of the eight victims identified as Bilal Khan, Sanaullah, Jalibeeb, Zakirullah, Salahuddin, Fazal Khan, Arif Khan and Junaid Khan were offered in their native Barkholozo area of Lowi Mamund tehsil.

Hundreds of people from different walks of life, including relatives of the victims, friends, fellow villagers and social and political activists attended the funerals, where photos of the deceased were displayed on large flex banners.
Local residents, including relatives of some victims, told reporters that although the bodies have not yet been recovered, they fear that their loved ones had surely died in the boat incident.

stories.title: 26th and 27th amendments ‘paralysed’ judiciary, alleges Insaf Lawyers Forum leader
summary: Mr Niazi said that they would launch a strong movement for rule of law and independence of judiciary, just like the lawyers had launched a historic movement for the independence of the judiciary during Gen Musharraf’s military government.

Niazullah Niazi says lawyers will launch movement for rule of law He stated that no grouping would be tolerated in ILF and it would be made united, organised and active in accordance with Imran Khan’s vision.
He appealed to lawyers all over Pakistan to play their role for the success of the nominated candidates of ILF.

stories.title: AJK rolls out Rs15bn 100-day action plan
summary: Transport and civic facilities Minister for Forests and Wildlife Waqar Ahmad Noor said 75 electric buses would be introduced in seven AJK cities under the Kashmir Express Service.

Jagran-II project Separately, Prime Minister Iftikhar Gillani told the AJK Legislative Assembly that his government was exploring options to complete the 48-megawatt Jagran-II hydropower project in Neelum Valley, where work has remained stalled due to multiple factors.
Mr Gillani said completion of the project remained among the government’s priorities and would boost electricity generation and revenue for AJK.

stories.title: Cricket Australia widens 'Sandpapergate' forum to 2017-2018 Ashes
summary: In a surprise development, the terms of reference released on Friday broadened to include “ball-management practices” during the 2017-2018 season, including the home Ashes series which Australia won 4-0.

In the wake of the South Africa fallout, England great Alastair Cook, who was part of the Ashes side, was asked whether the team suspected Australia of ball-tampering. “Yes a little bit, certainly in Perth when the outfield was wet with rain they got the ball-reversing,” he said.

She will investigate the Ashes, all four Tests of the South Africa tour, the events of March 24, 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught with sandpaper, and the conduct of the 2018 Cricket Australia probe.

stories.title: Two suspected robbers gunned down in Karachi's Buffer Zone ‘encounter’
summary: A police spokesperson said four armed robbers barged into a house in Sector 15-A-3, held the family members at gunpoint and started collecting valuables.
However, someone informed police, who rushed to the scene and challenged the robbers.
The spokesperson said the robbers tried to escape under the cover of firing and in the ensuing exchange of gunfire, two of them were killed while their accomplices managed to escape.

stories.title: Police van overturned as Larkana protest over double murder turns violent
summary: LARKANA: A large group of enraged people damaged and toppled a police mobile van while protesting over a gun attack on their community members on the outskirts of Larkana on Thursday.

There were conflicting accounts of the episode with the victims’ relatives and other community members claiming that the assailants were highwaymen and the area police attributing the attack to an old enmity between the victims and the assailants.
Enraged over the attack and suspected collusion between the police and assailants, the protesters vented their anger on the police team present at Otha Chowk during the sit-in.

stories.title: Woman hurt in acid attack in North Karachi
summary: KARACHI: A woman social worker was injured in an acid attack in North Karachi, officials said on Thursday.

Central SSP Dr Mohammed Imran Khan told Dawn that the woman, identified as Nazia Mohammed Ali, 38, was riding a motorcycle and passing by a public school in Sector 11-C 2 in North Karachi when a man attacked her with acid and fled.
She named Tabish Ali as the person who threw acid on her, stating that a few days ago she had recorded a statement against his father in a court of law.

stories.title: Punjab govt to build 1m houses in five years, says CM Maryam
summary: LAHORE: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz announced that the government would build one million houses over the next five years under the Apni Chhat Apna Ghar programme, following a directive from PML-N President Nawaz Sharif.

She said the Apni Chhat Apna Ghar programme was not merely the largest low-cost housing initiative in south Punjab, Punjab, Pakistan or Asia, but had emerged as the world’s most affordable housing programme.
The chief minister conferred PhD degrees upon 15 scholars and awarded gold medals to five students, acknowledging their academic excellence and remarkable achievements.

stories.title: Two men get three-month rigorous imprisonment each for attacking woman in Lahore
summary: Magistrate Hamidul Rahman Nasir, heading Model Criminal Court for Minor Offences, convicted the accused persons, Imran and Rizwan, under Section 352 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) (assault without grave and sudden provocation).
The magistrate found the complainant’s account of slapping consistent and convicted the two accused under a lesser offence by invoking Section 237 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The third accused, Tariq, was acquitted because the complainant, in the cross-examination, attributed the act of slapping only to Imran and Rizwan.

stories.title: Greed, official negligence and the collapse
summary: One resident, expressing anger over the incident, asked how a building approved for ground-plus-one construction could have reached six storeys.

Residents say structure approved for ground-plus-one construction could not have risen to six storeys without authorities’ knowledge He asked whether the relevant authority had challenged the stay order before a higher court.

Bungalows replaced by flats Speaking to Dawn, another resident said that over the past decade there had been a sharp rise in the conversion of bungalows approved for ground-plus-one construction into multiple portions and flats in the admin society.

stories.title: Six kids among 11 dead as car rams into trolley on Toba-Chichawatni Road
summary: TOBA TEK SINGH: Eleven persons of a family, including six children, died when their car rammed into a tractor-trolley from behind near Chak 268 GB on Toba-Chichawatni Road on Thursday night.
According to Rescue 1122, all 11 people travelling in the car belonged to the same family and were residents of Chak 66 GB, Tandlianwala.
All occupants of the car received critical injuries and six of them succumbed to their wounds on the spot when the speeding car rammed into the maize- loaded tractor-trolley.

stories.title: Big fat wedding in India draws 400,000 guests
summary: PATNA: Some 400,000 guests attended a wedding hosted by a politician in India’s poorest state, choking roads and sending spectators scrambling up electricity pylons for a glimpse of the lavish celebrations.
The event in Anant Singh’s native village of Nadawan drew such huge crowds that roads leading to the venue ground to a standstill.
Images published by the Press Trust of India news agency showed thousands jostling for a glimpse of the sprawling venue, while others perched precariously atop trees and electricity towers.

summary: LHC dissolves woman’s marriage on ground of physical, mental cruelty

stories.title: Constitutional liability
summary: EVERY out-of-school child is a living reminder to the state of its constitutional commitment, and these reminders have been increasing since the inception of Pakistan.
While these countries have made considerable progress in expanding educational access, Pakistan continues to struggle with millions of children excluded from the education system.

The question is therefore not simply how much it would cost to educate the excluded children, but why a country that has constitutionally guaranteed education to every child has failed to develop a sustainable financing mechanism to fulfil that guarantee.

stories.title: More credit, fewer women
summary: Sakina’s milk delivery records could give the bank a place to start.
Could we use the records buyers already keep to show what women like Sakina actually sell and earn?
A provincial livestock department could bring milk buyers and banks together to work with women who already run dairy businesses and want to expand.

stories.title: 16 laws enacted to strengthen law and order: Balochistan CM Bugti
summary: QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti has said his government has enacted 16 laws to strengthen the law and order situation and improve security-related matters in the province.
He said the provincial government stands shoulder to shoulder with security forces in the fight against terrorism.
He said that a strong and effective administrative structure was essential for addressing security challenges and resolving public issues.

stories.title: Makers step up rollout of electric bikes
summary: KARACHI: Amid the falling trend in petrol prices, a growing number of stakeholders have stepped up efforts to test their new electric bikes in the market.

Subsidy on purchase of bikes The Punjab government has decided to provide a subsidy of Rs50,000 for the purchase of electric bikes, while the Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification programme (PAVE) has also offered a subsidy of Rs80,000.
Mohammad Sabir Shaikh, an expert on bikes, said assemblers are testing their luck in the electric market.

stories.title: Opposition disarray
summary: THE PTI on Wednesday distanced itself from Mahmood Khan Achakzai’s proposal for a national government and his demand for political and constitutional reforms.
The opposition would be better off using the rest of the parliamentary term to press the government on issues that bear directly on democratic governance.
Sustained engagement in parliament would help the opposition build public confidence, and it should not squander that chance on premature demands for another political arrangement.

stories.title: Amid talk of new provinces, Sindh CM announces consultations on local govt empowerment
summary: Addressing a press conference at the CM House, the chief minister said that the aim was to strengthen local bodies, give them greater autonomy and improve their financial and administrative capacity.

Flanked by provincial ministers Sharjeel Memon, Nasir Shah, Saeed Ghani and Ziaul Hassan Lanjar and Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab, the chief minister added that the committee would consult political parties, civil society and other relevant stakeholders.
The chief minister said that the province had held elections even in difficult political and security conditions. “We want to make local bodies more empowered.

stories.title: Tevez hopes Ronaldo will join Messi at testimonial
summary: Former Argentina striker Carlos Tevez said Thursday Lionel Messi would appear in his testimonial next month and that he was confident Cristiano Ronaldo would be playing alongside them.
The 42-year-old Tevez played with Messi for Argentina and also lined up with Ronaldo at Manchester United.
Tevez started his career at Boca Juniors and returned there in 2018 before retiring four years later, and now his testimonial will be played December 20 at their Bombonera stadium in Buenos Aires.

stories.title: Jodar sends Spain into Davis Cup semi-final clash with Britain
summary: Rafael Jodar fought back from behind to send Spain past Austria and set up a Davis Cup semi-final meeting with Britain on Thursday.

Spain were leading the tie in Bologna 1-0 when Jodar lost his first set to Austrian Jurij Rodionov, but then closed out the match and the quarter-final, losing only one game in two sets for a 2-6, 6-0, 6-1 triumph.
Spain captain David Ferrer said Alcaraz, who has won three consecutive individual titles including last week's ATP Finals, may be able to play in the singles against Britain on Saturday.

stories.title: Thanksgiving storm knocks out power, disrupts flights on US East Coast
summary: A powerful storm disrupted the Thanksgiving holiday along much of the United States East Coast on Thursday, knocking out power to nearly one million customers at one point as wind gusts of up to 70 mph (112 kph) toppled trees and power lines.
Wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph were reported or forecast across parts of Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, New Jersey, New York, and coastal New England, according to the US National Weather Service.

Officials had already postponed Thursday's 100th edition of the annual Macy's ​Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City because of the storm threat, the first time the event has been rescheduled due to severe weather.

stories.title: Kenya breached constitution by allowing US-backed Ebola quarantine site, court says
summary: A Kenyan court ruled on Thursday that the government had breached parts of the constitution in allowing the construction of a United States-backed Ebola quarantine facility at a military air base in central Kenya, a project that has sparked deadly protests.
The 50-bed tented facility, located inside Laikipia Air Base near the central Kenyan town of Nanyuki, was intended to quarantine people exposed to the Ebola virus, including US citizens.
The government has said the facility is meant to support Ebola preparedness and to isolate or quarantine people exposed to the virus as part of wider public health contingency planning.

stories.title: Fatima Sana, Sadia Iqbal lead PCB women’s central contracts
summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has announced the central contracts for eight women cricketers for the 2026-27 season, with Fatima Sana and Sadia Iqbal featuring in Category A.
Muneeba Ali Siddiqui, Nashra Sundhu and Sidra Amin have been placed in Category B in recognition of their consistent performances and contributions across formats.
Category A: Fatima Sana, Sadia Iqbal Category B: Muneeba Ali Siddiqui, Nashra Sundhu, Sidra Amin Category C: Ayesha Zafar, Gull Feroza, Sadaf Shamas

stories.title: Karachi building collapse: Death toll rises to seven as rescue efforts continue
summary: The death toll from the collapse of an under-construction six-storey building in Karachi's Administrative Society rose to seven on Friday after three more bodies were recovered from the rubble, rescue officials said.

The investigating officer (IO) informed the court that permission had been granted for the construction of a ground-plus-one-storey building, but six storeys were being constructed in violation of the approved plan.
One of the suspects maintained that they had been produced before the court as though they were the building's owners.
